name: Purply Pink
lede: Purply Pink is a bright, purple-leaning pink from the xkcd color survey, close in hue to orchid but pulled warmer and brighter.

sections.title: A crowd name, not a system name
sections.body:
Purply Pink is built from ordinary English grammar, not a dye or a pigment: "purply" plus "pink" [1]. It comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, where over two million online respondents typed free-text names for randomly shown swatches, and this phrase was common enough to be kept as its own entry [1][2].

The ISCC-NBS system, built from older paint and textile samples, calls this hue block a brilliant purple, and our library's nearest professionally named neighbor is [[orchid]], 4.1 CIEDE2000 units away, a close but not identical match [2][3]. Unlike [[pink]] or [[purple]], which are among the eleven basic English color words, Purply Pink has no dictionary entry, no plate number and no recorded first use [1]. It sits on the [[magenta]] side of the pink-purple boundary that separates the two parent families [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive shows this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of it, as photographed [4]. That describes the gap between a 2010 internet-survey hue and five centuries of oil paint, not the color itself [4]. Measured in LCH, it is lightness 67, chroma 72, hue 330 degrees [3].

origin.named_after: descriptive combination of purple and pink
